# Warnings

@difference Extension: `blitzcc` has warnings with levels (`-W0` to `-W4`), `-W<name>` and `-Wno-<name>` options and `-Werror`; the original has none.

`blitzcc` points out code that is legal but probably not what was meant. A warning looks like an error, names the option that controls it, and often adds a `notice:` line that says how to fix it:

```
program.bb:1:12: warning: Implicit conversion from Float32 to Int32, the fractional part is lost. [-Wimplicit-lossy-real-to-int]
Local i% = 2.5
           ^^^ HERE
notice: Use Int(value) to convert on purpose, or SatInt(value) to stop at the limits of Int32.
```

The carets under the line cover the part of the code the message is about (a single one when it is a point), and the dashes after them reach to the end of the line. A *notice* is also a warning that is only a hint, such as a variable that is never used; its first line says `notice:` instead of `warning:`.

Warnings about implicit conversions name both types, with their long names (`Int8` to `Int64`, `UInt8` to `UInt64`, `Float16`, `Float32`, `Float64` and `String`), and the `notice:` line names the function that converts on purpose: `Int`, `Float`, `Str`, `Byte`, `UShort`, `Long`, `Double` and so on, and for whole numbers also the `Sat` version (`SatInt`, `SatByte`, ...) that stops at the limits instead of wrapping around.

Warnings never stop the compilation, unless they are turned into errors with `-Werror`. Errors (a program that can not be compiled) always stop it, and are printed as `file:line:column: error: ...` with the same source line display.

[[Blitz-Tidy]] fixes most of these warnings in your source files for you.

## Levels

`-W0` to `-W4` choose how many warnings there are: each level has all the warnings of the levels below it. `-W2` is the default.

| Level | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `-W0` | No warnings. |
| `-W1` | Code that loses information. |
| `-W2` | Likely mistakes (default). |
| `-W3` | Style, and notices about code that does nothing. |
| `-W4` | Declarations without a type, and notices about functions that are never called. |

## Options

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `-W0` ... `-W4` | Set the level. |
| `-W<name>` | Turn the warning `<name>` on, whatever the level is. |
| `-Wno-<name>` | Turn the warning `<name>` off, whatever the level is. |
| `-Werror` | Every warning that is on is an error: it is printed as `error: ... [-Werror=<name>]`, the whole program is still checked, and then `blitzcc` fails. Notices are not turned into errors. |
| `-Werror=<name>` | Only the warning `<name>` (a notice too) is an error, and it is turned on if the level does not include it. |
| `-Wno-error=<name>` | The warning `<name>` stays a warning with `-Werror`. |
| `-Wno-error` | Cancel an earlier `-Werror`. |

`-W<name>` and `-Wno-<name>` win over the level, and `-Werror=<name>` and `-Wno-error=<name>` win over `-Werror`, wherever on the command line they are. The options are not case sensitive. An unknown name is an error. `-q` hides warnings and notices (not the ones that are errors) and `+q` hides everything.

## The warnings

| Name | Level | Warns about |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `loop-iterator-type-unsafe` | 1 | A `For` loop whose variable is a real number (`Float`, `Half`, `Double`). Reals do not count exactly, so the loop can run once more or less than expected, or never end. |
| `large-local-array` | 1 | A `Local` array in a function that takes more than 4 KiB (1024 `Int` entries), which has to be made and set to 0 again on every call; above 64 KiB it lives on the heap. Make it once with `Global` or `Dim` outside of the function. The main program is not checked. |
| `implicit-lossy-int-to-int` | 1 | An integer assigned or passed to an integer that is smaller or has another sign (`Int` to `Byte`, `Int` to `UInt`, ...), which can change the number. A number written in the program that fits is fine. |
| `implicit-lossy-real-to-int` | 1 | A Float assigned or passed to an integer (`Local i% = 2.5`). It is rounded, like in the original, and the fractional part is lost. |
| `implicit-lossy-real-to-real` | 1 | A real number assigned or passed to a smaller one (`Double` to `Float`). |
| `implicit-string-to-number` | 1 | A String assigned or passed to a number. It is 0 if it does not start with a number. |
| `implicit-lossy-int-to-real` | 2 | An integer assigned or passed to a real number that can not hold all its values (`Int` to `Float`, `Long` to `Double`). |
| `implicit-variable` | 2 | A variable that was never declared with `Local`, `Global` or `Dim`. Blitz makes it a local one, so this is legal. |
| `return-missing-value` | 2 | `Return` without a value in a function that was declared with a type (`Function Name$()`, `Function Name:Float()`). It returns 0, `""` or `Null`. A function without a type is an `Int` by default, so it is left alone. |
| `return-type-mismatch` | 2 | `Return` gives a value of another type than the function was declared with (an `Int` in a function that returns a `String`, a `Double` in a `Float` one). Both types are named, with the conversion function that fixes it when there is one. A whole number written in the program that fits (`Return 0` in a `Float` function) is fine. When this is on, it says what the `implicit-*` warnings would say for that `Return`. |
| `unused-result` | 2 | A function that returns a value is called as a statement, and the value is thrown away. Built-in and `.decls` functions without a result, and functions of the program that never `Return` a value, do not warn. A call in an expression, `If` or `Select` is a use. |
| `implicit-number-to-string` | 3 | A number assigned or passed to a String. |
| `inout-parameter-unwritten` | 3 | A path of a function (a `Return`, or the end) leaves without writing to one of its `InOut` parameters, so the variable of the caller stays as it was. For an `Out` parameter this is an error. See [Parameter modes](Parameter-Modes). |
| `short-type-notation` | 3 | A type written as a character behind the name (`x%`, `x%%`, `x#`, `x##`, `x$`) instead of the long form (`x:Int32`, `x:Int64`, `x:Float32`, `x:Float64`, `x:String`). The long form is the one the language is documented with. `.TypeName` has no other form and does not warn. `blitz-tidy` can rewrite it. |
| `unreachable-code` (notice) | 3 | A statement after `Return`, `End`, `Goto` or `Exit` in the same block, which can never run. Labels and `Data` do not count. Only the first one is reported. |
| `unused-variable` (notice) | 3 | A `Local` or `Global` variable that is never read (writing to it does not count). It is optimized away. |
| `typeless-declaration` | 4 | A `Local`, `Global`, `Const`, `Dim`, `Function` (its result), function parameter or `Field` without a type (`Local x`, `Function Foo(a)`, `Field size`): it is an Int, which is not always what was meant. For a function the notice says which type its `Return` statements give (`:Void` if none gives a value). |
| `loop-unroll-requires-constant` | 4 | The `Step` of a `For` loop is not a constant, so the loop can not be unrolled. A constant step of 0 is an error. |
| `unused-function` (notice) | 4 | A function that is never called. It is optimized away. |

`blitzcc --help` lists the same warnings.

## Examples

```sh
blitzcc -W0 program.bb                  # no warnings at all
blitzcc -W4 -Werror -c program.bb       # strict: check the program, any warning fails (notices do not)
blitzcc -Werror -Wno-error=unused-result program.bb   # fail on warnings, except for unused-result
blitzcc -Wno-implicit-lossy-real-to-int program.bb    # the default level, without that warning
blitzcc -W4 -Werror=unused-function -c program.bb     # a notice that is an error
```
